title: Nutrient Interactions, Balance and Developmental Context

content.overview: Plant nutrition is an interacting system. Cannabis responses to N, P, K and other elements depend on concentration, ratios, growth stage, root-zone conditions and genotype, so a single nutrient number rarely explains crop performance by itself.

vocabulary.definition: A condition in which the supply or uptake of one element changes the response to another.
An interaction where increasing one ion can reduce uptake or availability of another.
Tissue or solution accumulation above the amount needed for maximum performance.

sections.title: Elements interact
sections.body: Controlled cannabis studies have measured significant N×K, K×P and higher-order interactions. Interpretation should therefore consider nutrient balance rather than treating each element independently.

sections.title: More input is not automatically more yield
sections.body: Recent root-zone research found that higher P and overall nutrient concentration could increase accumulation without improving yield or cannabinoid concentration under the tested conditions.

sections.title: Stage and system limit generalization
sections.body: A vegetative hydroponic response does not automatically define flowering, soil or all-cultivar requirements. Recommendations must preserve the conditions under which evidence was produced.

workedExamples: A rising P input paired with falling leaf Mg should trigger an interaction hypothesis rather than a conclusion that Mg was absent from the feed.
A high solution EC with no yield improvement may represent excess concentration rather than a hidden productivity opportunity.
commonMistakes: Treating fertilizer labels as crop requirements.
Increasing several nutrients at once after one symptom.
Copying a vegetative research target into flowering without validation.
content.practicalApplication: When evaluating a nutrition change, record stage, cultivar, source water, formulation, input EC/pH, root-zone trend and tissue response so nutrient effects remain interpretable.
content.summary: Advanced nutrition replaces single-number recipes with interaction-aware, stage-aware and system-aware reasoning.
